At least 14 people were killed and 20 others injured on Sunday when a suicide bomber struck outside the Kabal Police Station in Pakistan’s Swat district during a large public rally against terrorism, police officials said. The attacker detonated explosives after officers attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station, triggering panic among hundreds of demonstrators gathered nearby.The blast occurred near Kabal Chowk, where residents had assembled for the “Olasi Pasoon” peace gathering to demand an end to the recent resurgence of militant violence in the Swat Valley.Soon after the bombing, PTM Momand said its social media team was launching a campaign condemning the attack on what it described as a peaceful gathering.“PTM socialMediaTeam is launching a campaign to condemn the horrific bomb blast that targeted Apeaceful gathering of ‘Olasi Pasoon’ in Swat. People who assembled to demand peace wr met with violence instead. Initial reports indicate at least seven pple killed #StopStateTerrorismInSwat,” the group posted on X.Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi confirmed that 14 people had died in the explosion. Earlier, Swat Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain said seven people, including four police officers, had been killed and 20 injured, but the death toll was later revised upward.According to Swat District Police Officer Umar Khan, the bomber blew himself up after police personnel tried to search him at the station gate. He said security forces had cordoned off the area and launched an investigation to gather further evidence.The attack took place as the final speaker was addressing the gathering, causing widespread panic among those attending the rally. Rescue teams, police and local authorities rushed to the scene, and the injured were taken to Saidu Sharif Teaching Hospital for treatment. No group had claimed responsibility for the bombing by Sunday evening.Before the explosion, speakers at the rally had condemned the rise in militant activity and demanded that the government ensure lasting peace in the region. They said their movement had a single agenda, the restoration of peace and the elimination of terrorism from Swat.The speakers argued that maintaining law and order and eradicating terrorism were the responsibility of the state, and warned that continued insecurity could fuel broader public unrest. They also criticised the authorities for allegedly taking action against peaceful citizens while militants continued to operate in the mountainous areas of Swat.“Our children deserve education, and our families deserve to live in peace,” one speaker told the crowd.“We have witnessed years of bloodshed. Our mothers, sisters, and daughters have suffered immensely, and we do not want another generation of widows and orphans.”The bombing came amid a sharp increase in militant violence across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Earlier on Sunday, an improvised explosive device blast near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza injured two police officers in Peshawar. On 30 July, nine police officers were killed in an attack on a police checkpost in Hangu.According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 terrorism-related deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, an increase of 105 per cent.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the loss of life and called for a comprehensive investigation into the bombing. He directed the relevant authorities to provide the best medical facilities to those injured.“Terrorists will never succeed in their nefarious efforts to harm peace, national unity, and the writ of the state,” he said, adding that the sacrifices of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police were a “source of pride for the entire nation”.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the attack, saying, “Terrorists cannot demoralise the nation with cowardly attacks.”Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's chief minister Sohail Afridi sought a report from the provincial Inspector General of Police and offered condolences to the families of the victims. “The elements hostile to peace will never be allowed to succeed in their nefarious intentions,” he said.
Article Summary: At least 14 people were killed and 20 others injured when a suicide bomber struck outside the Kabal Police Station in Pakistan’s Swat district. The attacker detonated explosives after officers attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station. The blast occurred near Kabal Chowk, where residents had assembled for the ‘Olasi Pasoon’ peace gathering.

Article Title: Clarify Dhaka policy: Bangladesh to India after Hasina’s presser
Article Text:
Bangladesh’s state minister of foreign affairs Shama Obaed said India must decide whether it will continue to allow leaders of Awami League to 'carry out conspiratorial activities' from its territory.

A day after former Bangladesh PM and Awami League chief Sheikh Hasina virtually addressed a news conference in New Delhi, Bangladesh Thursday asked India to clarify its policy towards Dhaka.Bangladesh’s state minister of foreign affairs Shama Obaed said India must decide whether it will continue to allow leaders of Awami League to “carry out conspiratorial activities” from its territory.“India is a democratic country. India itself has to decide what their foreign policy will be regarding Bangladesh. We want good relations, in the interest of the people of both countries,” she said. “But the relationship has to be based on equality, with mutual respect and maintaining their own interests. If India understands that, it will be good for everyone,” she said.

Article Title: B’desh student party leaders accuse Hasina of trying to create unrest from Indian soil
Article Text:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, center, looks at an exhibit at the inauguration of a museum which will serve as a memorial for those killed during the mass uprisings in July 2024, at the former residence of Bangladesh's ousted leader Sheikh Hasina, in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Wednesday

Dehradun:

National Citizen Party, formed by student leaders who led the anti-Sheikh Hasina mass movement in 2024, has accused the ousted former Bangladesh PM of trying to create unrest in the country from Indian soil after she declared at a news conference in New Delhi that she would return in Dec.Ariful Islam Adeeb, senior joint convener of NCP, told TOI from Dhaka on Thursday that Hasina and Awami League had lost political relevance after she fled Bangladesh, and that her latest remarks were aimed at disturbing the situation back home. “After fleeing the country, she and her party, Awami League, have become politically insignificant. Now, by making such statements from India, she is not just trying to create unrest but also ruining bilateral relations between the two countries,” Adeeb said.The reaction came a day after Bangladesh’s ministry of foreign affairs issued a strongly worded statement condemning Hasina’s media interaction in New Delhi. “Bangladesh is outraged that the absconding convicted genocider Sheikh Hasina was allowed this evening to engage in live interaction with the media in New Delhi where she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against Bangladesh and her people,” the ministry said.NCP, founded after the July Uprising that forced Hasina from power, said her remarks were also an attempt to put pressure on the elected govt by creating the possibility of a law-and-order situation through her supporters who remained in hiding. “Hasina is convicted for mass atrocities and killings during her 15 years of rule. Now, she is trying to put pressure on a democratically elected govt by keeping it on its toes to tackle possible law-and-order problems that may be created by her supporters. But NCP, like every other citizen of Bangladesh, will never allow that to happen,” Adeeb said.Bangladesh MFA also said Hasina’s interaction had come on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an insult to those who died during the uprising. “On a day when the people of Bangladesh are observing the second anniversary of the July Revolution, this interaction by Sheikh Hasina on Indian soil stands as an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and a grievous insult to the martyrs of July Revolution,” the statement said.While NCP and Hasina’s other political rivals described her as politically irrelevant, some independent observers said Awami League and its former leader still remained central to Bangladesh’s political calculations. Md Saiful Alam Chowdhury, associate professor in the department of mass communication and journalism at University of Dhaka, said Hasina’s possible return could alter the political mood.“Hasina is the elephant in the room, which nobody wants back in the country. Every political rival, including ruling BNP, knows very well that the day she returns to Bangladesh, there will be tremors in the political scenario. The very evidence of it is the reaction from govt and parties to her decision to return,” Chowdhury said.He added that Hasina’s return would put smaller parties and even the ruling formation under pressure. “Parties like NCP and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami will exist only on paper if she returns. BNP will also become vulnerable as Hasina will hog the limelight in the media and on the international stage. As of now, the country can only wait and watch her next actions,” Chowdhury said.
Article Summary: National Citizen Party, formed by student leaders who led the anti-Sheikh Hasina mass movement in 2024, has accused the ousted former Bangladesh PM of trying to create unrest in the country. Ariful Islam Adeeb, senior joint convener of NCP, told TOI from Dhaka on Thursday that Hasina and Awami League had lost political relevance.
